lawyer:
A. K. M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on-Record.  ------ For the Petitioners. 
Md. Osman Ghani, Advocate, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record.  ------ For the Respondents.

Md. Layek Khan and another ------ Petitioners.
Vs.

full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Aziz J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 17.04.2008 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2727 of 2003 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 19th May, 2003 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet, in Small Cause Suit No. 9 of 1999 decreeing the same. 

 4. Trial Court after hearing the case and examining the evidence on record and: perusing the agreement and documents decreed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 19.05.2003. 

 5. Being aggrieved by dissatisfied with the above judgment and decree, the defendant-petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 2727 of 2003 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division upon hearing the parties discharged the Rule vide judgment and order dated 27.04.2008. Hence this leave petition by the petitioners. 

 6. Mr. Md. Osman Ghani, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that trial Court and also the High Court Division while decreeing the suit failed to appreciate that admittedly the defendants have been paying rent as per the existing rate and as such they are not the defaulter; but in spite of that the trial Court decreed the suit and the revisional Court without considering the vital aspect of the case affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court mechanically and in a slip short manner. He further submits that the High Court Division while discharging the Rule failed to consider that according to the judgment of the trial Court, the defendants have paid enhanced rent regularly, but the trial Court decreed the suit as the plaintiff refused to accept enhance rent of the suit premises, but in case of refusal to enhance the rent, the plaintiff has option to take resort for enhance of rent under Section 15 of the Rent Control Act, 1991 and as such the decree passed by the trial Court on the ground of non payment of standard rent as affirmed by the revisional Court is not sustainable. He also submits that revisional application has been filed under Section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act, the High Court Division ought to have consider the matter with wider amplitude, but the revisional Court failed to discuss any of the grounds agitated by the petitioners, which is against the provisions of law. His further submission is that trial Court and the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the defendants have been paying standard rent of the suit premises but the Senior Assistant Judge without any basis held that the defendants were not agreeable to pay standard rent of the suit premises. Learned Advocate lastly submits that the High Court Division while decreeing the suit failed to take notice that in the original agreement rent was fixed at Tk. 120/- but due to plaintiff's undue pressure and insistence defendants were compelled to increase the rent upto Tk. 250/- but the trial Court failed to appreciate those aspect of the case and held that the rent paid by the defendants was not standard rent. The trial Court did not specify the which is standard rent for the suit promises and as such the trial Court arrived at a wrong conclusion. 

 8. The trial Court decreed the suit directing the defendant-petitioners to vacate the suit premises within 30 days finding the defendant-petitioner as defaulters on due consideration of facts and evidence of the case both oral and documentary and holding that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division affirmed the judgment of the trial Court on discussion and consideration of the evidence and material on record of the case. The learned Single Judge having discharged the Rule on proper finding based on evidence and materials on record we find no reason to disturb the same. Hence this leave petition is dismissed having no merit.
